edits.name: Gemini CLI
edits.old: The open-source answer to Claude Code, and the one to reach for when cost is the constraint. The free tier runs 1,000 requests a day on a Google sign-in, no card. It streams the terminal state rather than asking permission before each change, so it moves faster but watches you less closely. Keep Claude Code for production work where verification matters, and run Gemini CLI for cheap one-shot passes over a large codebase. Worth knowing both. GAP add, June 2026.

edits.name: Dify
edits.old: The low-code AI app builder for people who don't want to touch code. Drag nodes onto a canvas, wire in Claude or GPT, point it at your documents and it handles the chunking and embedding itself with no manual tuning. That automatic knowledge base is the real differentiator. The self-hosted version is free with no meaningful limits. If n8n is the automation workhorse, Dify is where a non-technical team ships a working agent in an afternoon. GAP add, June 2026.

edits.name: Floot
edits.old: GAP: this directory has three other app builders and has never had the one reviewers keep holding up as the direct Lovable comparison. Floot builds and hosts a complete app, backend, database, and authentication included, from a single conversation, and the all-in credit model means you are not juggling separate hosting and database bills the way you can with Lovable. It has real traction: 623 upvotes and a 4.9-star rating on Product Hunt, and reviewers consistently flag stronger error handling and fewer stuck-in-a-loop moments than competitors. It has been quietly building a reputation since 2025, so this is a gap the directory should have closed sooner, not a new arrival. The trade-off is a single all-in Pro tier at £19 a month rather than Lovable's cheaper entry point, and less granular control once you need something genuinely custom.

edits.name: Zo Computer
edits.old: A personal AI cloud computer: your own always-on server with an agent that manages files, runs code, and hosts small apps and sites from a single chat interface. It graduates from the watch list this run on the strength of a genuine Product Hunt listing, 202 upvotes and a five-star rating from three reviews, alongside its original There's an AI for That mention, the second independent source it was missing last time. The free tier includes 100GB storage and one hosted project; paid tiers start from £13/mo. The pitch is real ownership: your data and tools live on infrastructure you control rather than scattered across five subscriptions, and it sits in the same territory as Manus and OpenClaw, an AI that runs your digital life rather than just answering questions. It suits someone comfortable enough with the idea of a personal server to appreciate what that buys them; it is not yet a one-click product for a non-technical reader. Worth trying if you want a genuinely personal AI infrastructure layer rather than another chat window.

edits.name: Adobe Creative Cloud
edits.old: Worth it if someone in the building already knows these tools, and hard to justify if nobody does. For exhibition graphics, print, or anything where typography has to be right, there's still no substitute, and the generative features inside Photoshop and Illustrator sit in the workflow rather than sending you somewhere else. Charity Digital Exchange is the route to the discount and it's a meaningful one. If your output is mostly social and mostly fast, Canva will serve you better and cost you nothing.
